groups.title: Outcome
groups.subtitle: What quantity is recorded for each observation?

options.label: Binary outcome (0 or 1)
options.hint: An event indicator. Compare probability-point and nonlinear probability models.

options.label: Nonnegative count
options.hint: Events counted over a defined exposure period.

options.label: Fraction or share (0 to 1)
options.hint: A proportion with a stated denominator; boundaries may occur.

options.label: Time to an event
options.hint: Event times with a defined risk period and possible censoring.

groups.title: Observation structure
groups.subtitle: Does the same unit appear at multiple times?

options.label: One record per unit
options.hint: A cross-section, or distinct units in repeated cross-sections.

options.label: Repeated records per unit
options.hint: Establish identifiers, time ordering and within-unit variation.

groups.title: Purpose and proposed design
groups.subtitle: What would justify the interpretation you want?

options.label: Association or prediction
options.hint: Specify the target population and sample; a useful association need not be causal.

options.label: Causal design unresolved
options.hint: Identify the confounding or selection mechanism before choosing a remedy.

options.label: Randomized assignment
options.hint: Check assignment, compliance, attrition and interference. Assignment effects and receipt effects differ.

options.label: Proposed excluded instrument
options.hint: Assess relevance, exclusion and exogeneity for the proposed instrument.

options.label: Before/after treatment comparison
options.hint: Assess untreated trends, timing, anticipation and spillovers.

groups.title: Sampling and dependence
groups.subtitle: Which observations may share unobserved shocks?

options.label: Independent observations
options.hint: Robust covariance allows unequal conditional variances; it does not repair confounding.

options.label: Independent clusters
options.hint: Name a cluster variable justified by sampling or assignment, and assess the number of clusters.

options.label: Complex survey design
options.hint: Weights, strata and primary sampling units require estimator-specific survey support.

options.label: Not established yet
options.hint: Resolve the covariance structure before interpreting standard errors or p-values.

ols.title: Linear regression
ols.why: A linear conditional-mean model or descriptive linear projection for a specified sample.
ols.diagnostic: Inspect functional form, influential observations and the covariance structure. Residual plots cannot establish exogeneity.
ols.scope: A linear conditional mean or a descriptive linear projection, in the stated outcome units.
assumptions: A causal slope needs a separate identification argument; a fitted regression does not supply one.
Inspect functional form and the observations contributing to each estimate.

logit.title: Logit
logit.why: Models binary outcomes with probabilities constrained to 0-1.
logit.stata:
logit y x1 x2, {vce}
margins, dydx(*)
logit.diagnostic: Report marginal effects and predicted probabilities.
logit.pitfall: Reading log-odds coefficients as probability-point changes, or treating fitted associations as causal.
logit.scope: The log-odds index is linear; the fitted response probability is nonlinear and bounded.
assumptions: Specify the conditional probability model and inspect separation and support.
A logit coefficient is a log-odds change. Average marginal effects and probabilities answer different questions.

count.title: Poisson and negative binomial
count.why: Poisson models a nonnegative exponential conditional mean; negative binomial adds a particular dispersion structure.
count.diagnostic: Study conditional dispersion, exposure and the process generating zeros. Poisson with robust inference does not require equal conditional mean and variance.
count.pitfall: Choosing NB from the unconditional variance alone, or treating many zeros as proof of a separate zero-generating process.
count.scope: Both model an exponential conditional mean; negative binomial adds a particular dispersion model.
assumptions: Define exposure and the process that produces zeros.
Poisson quasi-likelihood with a correctly specified mean and appropriate covariance does not require conditional mean–variance equality.

fractional.title: Fractional logit
fractional.why: Handles proportions between 0 and 1 without impossible predictions.
fractional.stata:
fracreg logit y x1 x2, {vce}
margins, dydx(*)
fractional.diagnostic: Inspect fitted values for boundary issues.
fractional.pitfall: Ignoring boundary values, the denominator or the sampling structure; a linear model is not automatically invalid.
fractional.scope: A conditional-mean model for responses in [0,1], including zero and one.
assumptions: State the denominator and whether observations are aggregates of different sizes.
A bounded nonlinear mean is a modeling choice; a linear projection is not automatically invalid.

hazard.title: Cox proportional-hazards model
hazard.stata:
stset duration, failure(event)
stcox x1 x2, {vce}
hazard.scope: A hazard model with a common multiplicative covariate effect; a hazard ratio is not a probability difference.
assumptions: Define risk entry, event coding, censoring and time scale before fitting.
Assess proportional hazards and whether censoring is plausibly independent conditional on the model.

panel.title: Linear unit and time fixed effects
panel.why: Linear unit fixed effects remove additive, time-invariant unit heterogeneity. They do not remove time-varying confounding.
panel.stata:
xtset id time
xtreg y x1 x2 i.time, fe {vce}
panel.diagnostic: Check within-unit variation, time effects, strict-exogeneity assumptions and dependence. A nonrejection in a Hausman test does not validate RE.
panel.pitfall: Treating unit FE as a general identification strategy, or clustering mechanically without considering the assignment and sampling design.
panel.scope: An alternative linear specification using within-unit changes after removing additive unit and time effects.
assumptions: Strict exogeneity of the idiosyncratic error with respect to the regressor history is a maintained condition of this static model.
Time-varying confounding, feedback and heterogeneous trends can remain. Time-invariant coefficients are not identified by within-unit changes.

iv.title: Linear instrumental variables
iv.why: A candidate only when relevant excluded instruments and a credible exclusion/exogeneity argument are available.
iv.diagnostic: Report the first stage and assess weak identification using procedures appropriate to the model and covariance. F > 10 is not a universal guarantee.
iv.pitfall: Treating a statistical test as proof of instrument validity or claiming finite-sample unbiasedness for 2SLS.
iv.scope: This is a linear IV specification, not an instrumented logit, count or hazard model.
assumptions: The excluded instrument must supply relevant variation and satisfy a defensible exclusion/exogeneity restriction.
Under heterogeneous effects, define the target and any additional conditions needed for its interpretation.

did.title: Two-group, two-period difference-in-differences
did.why: A candidate design for treatment and comparison groups observed before and after adoption, under an appropriate parallel-trends assumption.
did.diagnostic: Study assignment, anticipation, spillovers and untreated trends. Pre-trend nonrejection cannot establish parallel trends.
did.pitfall: Applying the simple two-period specification to staggered adoption with heterogeneous effects without checking the estimand.
did.scope: A simple comparison of changes in the outcome mean. Binary outcomes are measured in probability points; count outcomes remain in count units.
assumptions: Parallel untreated mean trends, no anticipation and an appropriate no-interference condition are required for the intended treatment effect.
Treatment timing, composition changes and staggered adoption can require a different estimator or estimand.

diagnostics.title: Model-specific diagnostics
diagnostics.why: Checks can reveal contradictions and misspecification; no checklist certifies identification.
diagnostics.stata:
* OLS illustration: hettest requires conventional VCE.
regress y x1 x2
estat hettest
estat vif
rvfplot
diagnostics.diagnostic: Use postestimation commands documented for the fitted estimator. These OLS commands do not apply to every model above.
diagnostics.pitfall: Using passing tests as proof of exogeneity, normality, valid instruments or the correct functional form.
diagnostics.scope: These commands illustrate OLS postestimation only; they are not an all-model checklist.
assumptions: A test of a maintained model restriction is not a test of every identifying assumption.

reporting.title: Reporting the comparison
reporting.why: Translate estimates into plain-language results and tables.
reporting.diagnostic: State units, sample restrictions, estimand, uncertainty, identification assumptions and material limitations.
reporting.pitfall: Only reporting p-values without effect size context.
reporting.scope: State the estimand, units, estimation sample and covariance alongside the coefficient.
assumptions: Separate what the data show from the assumptions needed to interpret it.

lpm.title: Linear probability model
lpm.why: OLS can be used with a binary outcome. Its slopes describe probability-point differences under a linear mean specification, or coefficients of a linear projection.
lpm.scope: A 0/1 outcome does not prohibit OLS. Predictions can leave [0,1], and a linear slope imposes a particular approximation.
assumptions: Probability-point interpretation concerns a change in a conditional mean or linear projection; it is not automatically a causal effect.
With a nonconstant response probability, binary-outcome errors are generally heteroskedastic.
lpm.diagnostic: Inspect fitted probabilities and whether a constant slope is a useful approximation over the relevant support.
lpm.pitfall: Rejecting every linear model solely because the outcome is binary, or ignoring implausible extrapolation.

panelCount.title: Poisson with unit effects
panelCount.why: An exponential mean can include unit effects instead of treating repeated counts as a pooled sample. Conditional fixed-effects Poisson and a Poisson fit with unit indicators provide two implementations.
panelCount.scope: Within-unit variation identifies time-varying slopes. A unit-indicator fit may be costly with many units.
assumptions: The conditional-mean and exogeneity restrictions must hold. Unit effects do not remove time-varying confounding.
Inspect units with no events, exposure and the effective estimation sample.
panelCount.stata:
xtset id time
* vce(robust) here allows dependence within each panel.
xtpoisson y x1 x2 i.time, fe vce(robust)
panelCount.diagnostic: Identify dropped units and the variation remaining within units.
panelCount.pitfall: Treating a count-model fixed effect or a cluster adjustment as a general remedy for endogeneity.
